summary: Craig’s cumulative creator, morality, and resurrection case met Law’s stronger suffering evidence and evil-God symmetry challenge, which remained insufficiently distinguished by providential skepticism.

pro.text: therefore the universe has a Transcendent cause
pro.context: Craig presents this conclusion as deductively following from the universe’s beginning and the premise that whatever begins has a transcendent cause.

con.text: there's far far too much good stuff in the world
con.context: Law grants possible defenses of an evil creator but argues that abundant goodness still permits its observational exclusion, establishing his parity challenge.
